🔒 CWE-693 OWASP:A05-Injection CVSS:7.5 | This Express app renders documents to a browser but never mounts helmet. Without it the responses carry no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or referrer policy, so any rendered page is framable and unconstrained. | HIGH
   Fix: Add helmet middleware: app.use(helmet()). Install with 'npm install helmet'. | https://helmetjs.github.io/

🔒 CWE-798 OWASP:A04-Cryptographic CVSS:9.8 | Hard-coded Session secret detected | CRITICAL [SOC2,PCI-DSS,HIPAA,GDPR]
   Fix: Use environment variable: process.env.SESSION_SECRET or secret management service | https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html

🔒 CWE-89 OWASP:A03-Injection CVSS:9.8 | SQL statement built from "req.body.login" and executed. An attacker controls part of the statement text. | CRITICAL [SOC2,PCI-DSS,NIST-CSF]
   Fix: Pass the value as a bound parameter (`$1` / `?`) instead of concatenating it into the statement. | https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/SQL_Injection

🔒 CWE-78 OWASP:A05-Injection CVSS:9.8 | Shell command built via string concatenation or template literal. An attacker who controls any interpolated value can execute arbitrary OS commands. | CRITICAL [SOC2,PCI-DSS,ISO27001,NIST-CSF]
   Fix: Use spawn(cmd, [arg1, arg2]) with separate arguments instead of exec(cmd + args). Never build shell commands via string interpolation. | https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/OS_Command_Injection_Defense_Cheat_Sheet.html

🔒 CWE-601 OWASP:A01-Broken CVSS:6.1 | res.redirect() receives a value directly from req.query, which is user-controlled. An attacker can redirect victims to a malicious site. | HIGH
   Fix: Validate the redirect target against an allowlist of trusted paths/origins, or use a relative path that cannot be redirected off-domain. | https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Unvalidated_Redirects_and_Forwards_Cheat_Sheet.html

🔒 CWE-502 OWASP:A08-Software CVSS:9.8 | Unsafe deserialization of untrusted data (incl. model/tool output) | HIGH
   Fix: Use JSON.parse() or validated safe deserialization libraries | validate model/tool output via schema and size limits | https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html

🔒 CWE-611 OWASP:A05-Injection CVSS:9.1 | External entity processing is enabled | CRITICAL
   Fix: Disable external entity processing | https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/611.html

🔒 CWE-598 | Query parameter 'token' is sensitive. Query strings are stored in access logs, proxy logs, browser history and leak via the Referer header. | MEDIUM
   Fix: Move the value to the POST request body (req.body) or an Authorization header; never accept secrets via the query string. | https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/598.html

🔒 CWE-327 OWASP:A04-Cryptographic CVSS:7.5 | Use of weak hash algorithm: MD5. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for security purposes. | CRITICAL [PCI-DSS,HIPAA,ISO27001,NIST-CSF]
   Fix: Replace with sha256: crypto.createHash("sha256").update(data). If this hash is an identifier rather than a security control — an EVALSHA key, an ETag, a cache key — store it under one of the nonCryptographicNames instead. | https://owasp.org/www-community/vulnerabilities/Weak_Cryptography

findingsDetail.reason: Re-renders the reset form with req.query.token. A reset link carrying the token in the query string is how the feature is designed; the documented flaw is that the token is md5(login), not the transport. Arguable (morgan('tiny') logs full URLs), but not the documented or an independently proven exploit.
